description.p: Daak is a modern, lightweight email client inspired by Geary, focused on resource efficiency and a clean user experience.
Daakは、Gearyにインスピレーションを得た、リソース効率とクリーンなユーザー体験を重視したモダンで軽量なメールクライアントです。
Daak je moderní, nenáročný e-mailový klient inspirovaný aplikací Geary, zaměřený na efektivní využití systémových prostředků a čistý uživatelský zážitek.
Daak ist ein moderner, schlanker E-Mail-Client, inspiriert von Geary, mit Fokus auf Ressourceneffizienz und eine übersichtliche Benutzeroberfläche.
Daak est un client e-mail moderne et léger inspiré par Geary, axé sur l'efficacité des ressources et une expérience utilisateur épurée.
Daak è un client di posta elettronica moderno e leggero ispirato a Geary, focalizzato su efficienza delle risorse e un'esperienza utente pulita.
Daak er en moderne og lettvekt e-postklient inspirert av Geary, fokusert på effektiv ressursbruk og en ren brukeropplevelse.
Daak to nowoczesny, lekki klient poczty e-mail zainspirowany programem Geary, stawiający na wydajne wykorzystanie zasobów oraz przejrzysty interfejs użytkownika.
Daak é um cliente de e-mail moderno e leve, inspirado no Geary, com foco em eficiência no uso de recursos e uma experiência de uso limpa.
Daak, Geary'den esinlenen; kaynak verimliliğine ve temiz bir kullanıcı deneyimine odaklanan modern ve hafif bir e-posta istemcisidir.
Daak là ứng dụng email hiện đại và nhẹ, được lấy cảm hứng từ Geary, tập trung vào hiệu quả sử dụng tài nguyên và trải nghiệm người dùng gọn gàng.
Daak 是一款以 Geary 为灵感，注重资源效率与简洁使用体验的现代化轻量级电子邮件客户端应用程序。
Daak 是一款以 Geary 為靈感，注重資源效率與簡潔使用體驗的現代化輕量級電子郵件客戶端應用程式。
Daak 是一款以 Geary 為靈感，注重資源效率與簡潔使用體驗的現代化輕量級電子郵件客戶端應用程式。

ul.li: Eight more re-audit fixes, completing the re-audit: Mail Merge cancel now reports cancelled vs in-flight counts, contacts fall through to the next writable address book with failures surfaced, failed Mail Merge runs always offer Resume, a failed Sent save leaves a lasting Outbox warning instead of vanishing, settings-save failures name the failing setting and resync the dialog, non-English Outlook reactions are detected, the Mail Merge hourly cap gains an opt-in to count ordinary sends, and a blocked macOS notification permission is surfaced in Settings with a one-time notice

Ten more re-audit fixes: extension sign-in refreshes are single-flight per account so no false re-sign-in prompt, failed token saves fail loudly instead of poisoning the next refresh, cancelling a sign-in no longer kills the retry, restart Undo toasts can no longer be lost to the worker, moves clean up only after the destination sync confirms the copy, bad signatures no longer show phantom attachments, single-occurrence edits work on OAuth calendars, a dead tray no longer strands the window, encrypted mail from search shows no phantom attachment, and truncated bodies from search are flagged

Ten re-audit fixes: daily contact sync retries failed changes instead of losing them, period sync no longer deletes old mail still on the server, Mail Merge Send now reuses one Message-ID and queue sends clear before the Sent save, moved messages no longer marked permanently failed, calendar conflicts catch cancellations, organiser, alarms and missing stamps, reactions replace instead of doubling, failed sends block re-send with a database rule, and attachment-only mails with failed text are flagged with a viewer Retry

Nineteen audit fixes: failed body downloads retry on Force Resync, Unsubscribe header injection closed and one-click unsubscribe verified, Mail Merge duplicate suppression, cancel and failure recording fixed, Undo toast reliable, window can no longer hide without a tray, Message-ID lookups bracket-insensitive, attachments save byte-identical, server-search attachments fixed, new-mail counts real arrivals, large messages flagged truncated, contacts checked across the sending account's address books, and sign-in refreshes serialised

Ten audit fixes: encrypted messages stay decryptable, CardDAV sync is atomic, empty-server and mass-delete safeguards, no more ghost deletions, CalDAV conflicts surface instead of overwriting, sync-period purge fixed, Empty Spam/Trash guarded, crash-safe sends with a stable Message-ID, queued drafts locked during undo, and header sync no longer wipes fetched bodies
Outlook fallback reaction emails now show as pills on the original message, and the highlighted row always matches the message open in the preview pane
The reaction email banner now renders as a pale-blue card with the sender's name in bold and a larger font, like Outlook's fallback
Reactions are now sent Outlook-style: the fallback text quotes the full original message under a banner, and reacting queues the reaction in the Outbox with Undo instead of greying out the picker
Sent and cancelled rows are deleted from the Outbox instead of kept as history — the Sent folder and the Mail Merge run log are the record
Right-clicking a Spam folder in the sidebar now offers Empty Spam, with the same confirmation as the message-list button
Fixed Windows toast notifications showing the raw app ID — toasts now show "Daak" with the Daak logo instead of "net.absons.daak" with a generic icon
Fixed the Windows tray menu never showing: the tray now runs on a dedicated locked OS thread, so clicks reach the menu — double-click opens the window and right-click shows the menu
Save new send recipients to the sending account's contacts (Google Contacts, Microsoft contacts, or the account's CardDAV address book), with a Settings toggle to turn it off
CardDAV auto-discovery: adding an IMAP account now finds and links its address book automatically when the provider runs one
Fixed the Flatpak build: regenerated the vendored Go modules so the unread badge's font packages are included — v0.7.28 shipped without the Flatpak builds; the badge now ships on every build
Unread badge: the unified-inbox unread count now shows on the macOS Dock icon, the Windows taskbar button and the tray icon (capped at 99+), with a Settings toggle to turn it off
Fixed attachments showing twice: the on-demand body fetch appended a second copy of a message's files; it now replaces the attachment set, and already-doubled rows are cleaned up on upgrade
Mac: fixed the tray crash for real — v0.7.25's fix was incomplete and "Open Daak" still segfaulted; the cause was the window:show event reaching Wails ExecJS on the main thread, not the native show
Mac: left-click on the menu-bar icon still shows the tray menu; Windows and Linux behaviour is unchanged
Mac: left-clicking the menu-bar icon now shows the tray menu; double-clicking it no longer crashes the app
Mac: showing the window from the tray or a second launch now runs on the main thread and skips the native show when the window is already visible
Mac: fixed a crash on launch when Run in Background was on — the tray icon is now created on the main thread, and a failed tray start never leaves the app hidden
Single-instance: a second launch during startup no longer loses its "show" command
Release files: DMGs, Windows installers and Linux tarballs now carry the version in their filenames
Build: fixed the macOS build failure (Objective-C removed from the tray's cgo preamble; pure C now)
Mac: fixed a crash on launch when Run in Background was on — the tray icon is now created on the main thread, and a failed tray start never leaves the app hidden
Single-instance: a second launch during startup no longer loses its "show" command
Release files: DMGs, Windows installers and Linux tarballs now carry the version in their filenames
Window: Daak now remembers whether it was maximized or restored, and reopens in that state
Send in background with Undo Send: Send closes the composer and queues the message in the Outbox with a 5-second undo window (changeable in Settings); Undo returns it to Drafts

System tray: the right-click menu now has Compose new message, Check mail now and Settings alongside Open Daak and Quit Daak; Compose and Settings show the window first, Check mail now syncs in the background
Sidebar: all accounts now start collapsed on launch — only the Unified section is expanded; expanding an account during a session still works but does not carry over to the next launch
System tray: double-clicking the tray icon now opens the Daak window; a single click does nothing, and right-clicking shows the menu (Open Daak, Quit Daak)
Flatpak: the Flatpak packages are back — v0.7.17 shipped without them because the vendored Go module list had not been regenerated after the new system-tray dependency was added
Windows installer: reinstalling while Daak is running now asks the running app to quit gracefully instead of failing instantly with a locked-file error
System tray icon: Daak now shows a tray icon whenever Run in Background is on, so a hidden window can be reopened from the tray
Windows installer: reinstalling while Daak is running now asks the running app to quit gracefully instead of failing instantly with a locked-file error
System tray icon: Daak now shows a tray icon whenever Run in Background is on, so a hidden window can be reopened from the tray
Sidebar: the divider between the Unified section and your accounts now keeps its last position when you quit and reopen Daak
Windows installer: upgrading now removes the previous install in the other scope, so there can never be two Daak installs side by side
New app icon: the Daak envelope now uses a mint-to-emerald gradient
Windows installer: if Daak will not stop, the installer now offers to force-quit it and continue; answering No keeps the manual Retry path, unchanged
Fixed the Windows release build: the release workflow now locates the NSIS compiler instead of assuming where it is installed
Windows installer is now per-user by default: installing just for you needs no administrator rights; installing for all users still asks for admin rights
Windows installer now closes a running Daak by itself before updating or uninstalling
Windows installer is now per-user by default: installing just for you needs no administrator rights; installing for all users still asks for admin rights
Windows installer now closes a running Daak by itself before updating or uninstalling
Attachments no longer silently disappear on Windows: attachment ids are now UUIDs instead of timestamps, so two attachments saved in the same instant can no longer collide and drop one
Attachments no longer show twice after a resync: re-fetching a message now replaces its attachment set instead of adding to it
Mac DMG background fixed: drawn at the window's exact size, so the title, tagline, tiles and drag arrow are all fully visible
Title bar shows the real Daak envelope logo instead of the generic icon
Unread dot now sits between the checkbox and the contact photo, fully visible
Also includes the v0.7.7 changes: restyled Mac DMG background and Windows setup installers only
Mac DMG background restyled: dark background with the Daak title, the app tile, a drag arrow and the Applications tile
Windows now ships the setup installer only — the plain portable exe is gone; the installers are named x64 and arm64
Bulk delete Undo: deleting several messages and pressing Undo now restores all of them, not just one
Selection bar: Mark read and Mark unread are now a single toggle button that follows the majority
Deleting an opened message now closes its view too — the tab closes, the dialog dismisses, and the separate popup window closes
Mac versions now ship as a DMG: open it and drag Daak onto the Applications shortcut — no more zip
Calendar: linking a Google account now includes calendar access, so the calendar works straight away with no separate calendar link step
Sidebar divider: it now snaps at the level where it starts hiding accounts or unified folders, and a section scrolls with a visible scrollbar when something in it is hidden
Archive, Delete and Undo fixed — archiving falls back to All Mail when there is no Archive folder, and Undo restores a message even seconds after it was moved
Sidebar: sections expand only from the chevron — clicking an account name or the Unified heading opens its inbox instead
Sidebar: the divider above the Accounts block drags up and down, and never hides accounts while they fit
The app logo is narrower than in v0.7.2 — width down 10%, height down 5%, back to the original height
The app logo is slightly shorter than in v0.7.1 — still a touch taller than the original
Settings dialog: the tab bar no longer overlaps the content below it
Dock icon: the new envelope logo now shows in the Dock instead of the old one
Double-click the title bar to maximize or restore the window
Message list: drag the divider as wide as you like, and drag it to the right edge to close the preview pane
The app logo is slightly taller
One-time passcodes: a chip on messages with a code copies it in one click, and the message is filed away in Trash
Needs attention: a strip above the message list flags one-time codes, travel changes, payment failures and delivery problems
Sidebar rework: unified folders on top, accounts docked at the bottom — click an account name for its inbox, expand it for its folders
Unsubscribe: one-click unsubscribe from mailing lists, like Gmail
Message translation: translate a message into your language, with offline language downloads so it works without a connection
Category tabs: switch between All, Personal and Automated messages
Daak is now licensed under AGPLv3
Renamed the app to Daak, with the new app ID net.absons.daak and repository github.com/absonsnet/daak; existing data and settings move to the new location automatically
Email reactions: react to any message with an emoji from a button in the message header; reactions are sent to the original sender and shown as pills under the message
Incoming reaction emails from Gmail are recognised and shown as reactions instead of appearing as separate emails
Mail Merge dialog no longer repeats the composer's From, To, Cc, Bcc, Reply-To and Subject fields
Window controls now follow the operating system and desktop environment: traffic-light buttons on the left on macOS and Ubuntu, on the right on Windows and GNOME/KDE/XFCE
Windows gets native-style glyph buttons instead of the traffic-light circles
New Settings option to force the buttons left or right (Auto by default)
Mail Merge: turn one draft into one personalised message per recipient, using the same {{...}} template syntax as Thunderbird's Mail Merge add-on
Recipient sources: CSV, JSON, XLSX, and all unified contacts
